page.title: Best USB-C Charger with Block and Cable (2026): UGREEN 65W vs Belkin, ESR, Anker
page.h1: Best USB-C charger with block and cable
page.desc: The best USB-C charger with a built-in cable is the UGREEN Nexode 65W Retractable: 60 W through a 2.3 ft reel, a 65 W port and USB-A. Belkin 67W, ESR 45W and Anker 35W compared.
page.intro:
Short answer. The best USB-C charger with block and cable is the UGREEN Nexode 65W Charger with Retractable USB-C Cable ({buy:ugreen-nexode-65w-retractable-cable-charger}): 60 W through its built-in 2.3 ft retractable cable, a 65 W USB-C port and a 22.5 W USB-A port in a 6.9 oz cube. That 60 W cable gives an iPhone 17 the full 28 W it can take (ChargerLab measured the phone peaking at 28 W) and runs a 13-inch MacBook Air, and UGREEN rates the reel for 25,000 pulls, which answers the most common complaint about retractable chargers: the reel jamming.

If you want a longer reach, the Belkin UltraCharge Retractable 67W pulls out 3.3 ft at the same list price, but it has no USB-A port, no independent reviews yet, and was out of stock at Belkin on 2026-11-06. Phone-only shoppers can save money and weight with the Anker Nano Charger 35W, a 3.9 oz block with a 2.3 ft reel that still covers an iPhone 17 or Pixel. For a phone or iPad with the longest cable from a brand we can verify, the ESR Xtend 45W ({buy:esr-xtend-45w-retractable-charger}) reels out 3.1 ft and does 45 W PPS for Galaxy phones. Two-laptop households or 16-inch MacBook Pro owners should step up to the UGREEN Nexode 100W Retractable ({buy:ugreen-nexode-100w-retractable-cable-charger}).

Why a built-in cable instead of a block plus a loose cable: the cable is the part that fails first in the Anker 20 W bundles owners complain about, and it is the part that gets left behind. A retractable charger also removes the counterfeit risk of the cheap 20 W "with cable" bundles on Amazon that Apple has sued over.

page.after:
What owners complain about

Across retailer reviews, deal forums and review aggregators, five problems come up again and again. The reel jams or stops retracting: a ShopSavvy summary of a Sharge 65 W retractable attributes about 56% of its criticism to the mechanism, a Baseus retractable cable owner reported a jam within weeks, and ReTrak's retractable chargers average 2.1 of 5 at Best Buy Canada for the same reason. The cable is too short: about 33% of the Sharge complaints, and 9to5Mac's main knock on the Anker 35W. The charger delivers less than the label: the Sharge unit measured 41 W instead of 65 W, and MacSources measured the UGREEN 65W's USB-A port at about 18 W instead of 22.5 W. Cheap 20 W block-and-cable bundles die early: six separate Anker 20 W bundle owners on Best Buy, Slickdeals and Trustpilot reported the cable or block failing within a year. Finally, people are surprised when a second device slows the first; every multi-port charger here splits its total, and the UGREEN 65W drops its USB-C port to 7.5 W the moment the USB-A port is used.

Which one by need

Phone plus laptop, one block for travel: UGREEN Nexode 65W Retractable. 60 W through the reel runs a MacBook Air or a 65 W Windows laptop, and the spare 65 W port takes a long cable at a desk. Longest cable at 65 W class: Belkin UltraCharge Retractable 67W, 3.3 ft and a 2-year warranty, once it is back in stock; it gives up the USB-A port. Phone only, smallest and cheapest: Anker Nano Charger 35W, 3.9 oz with a second USB-C port; 35 W is more than an iPhone 17 or Pixel 10 can draw. Phone or iPad with a longer reach, Galaxy 45 W: ESR Xtend 45W, 3.1 ft of braided cable and PPS. 16-inch laptop or two laptops: UGREEN Nexode 100W Retractable, 100 W through the reel and 65 W + 30 W when a phone joins.

Not recommended

Unbranded 20 W "charger with cable" bundles on Amazon: Apple's lawsuit over fakes sold there and the early-failure reports above make the few dollars saved a poor bet. Sharge's 65 W retractable charger: measured 41 W and the highest share of reel complaints we found. ReTrak retractable chargers: 2.1 of 5 at Best Buy Canada with the retractor breaking soon after purchase. Anker's 20 W bundles are fine chargers, but a separate cable is the part owners report dying first, so a built-in reel from Anker, UGREEN or ESR is the better buy at this price.

notes: RESEARCH. Query is a generic 'block + cable' shopper; retractable-cable chargers are the honest answer because the loose cable is what fails and gets lost. Pain points (sources counted, Reddit was not reachable via search): reel jams/breaks 4 (ShopSavvy Sharge ~56% of criticism, Slickdeals Baseus cable jam, Best Buy CA ReTrak 2.1/5, Counterpart reviewer); cable too short 4 (ShopSavvy ~33%, 9to5Mac Anker 35W, Verizon Belkin review, nullfake 1 m note); output below label 2 (Sharge 41 W, MacSources UGREEN USB-A 18 W); cheap 20 W bundle/cable dies within a year 6 (Best Buy x3, Slickdeals x2, Trustpilot x1, all Anker 20 W bundles); counterfeit Apple-style bundles 2 (Apple lawsuit, nullfake); port-split surprise 3 (Macworld, Cubed3, Hi-Tech Century); bulk/weight 4 (Macworld, 9to5Mac, MacSources, Root Nation); reel not replaceable 2. SEGMENTS: (1) phone + laptop traveler: UGREEN 65W retractable wins on verified 60 W cable + 65 W port + USB-A at $39.99 (storecheck search 2026-11-06, compare-at $49.99); Belkin 67W ($39.99 belkin.com, 3.3 ft, 2-yr) is the honest longer-cable rival but out of stock at Belkin until Nov 11 2026, no independent review found, no USB-A, and Belkin is not an approved program (Amazon-only for us, and amzcheck returns 429 today so no Amazon record). (2) phone only: Anker Nano 35W A2658 ($29.99 anker.com 2026-11-06, 110 g) wins on price/size; Amazon-only, named without buy token. (3) phone/iPad wanting longer cable or Galaxy 45 W PPS: ESR Xtend 45W ($42.99 storecheck search 2026-11-06, compare $49.99; 3.1 ft). (4) 16-inch laptop / two laptops: UGREEN 100W retractable ($50.99 storecheck search 2026-11-06, compare $59.99).
